## Summary

Starting master SHA: `96c6eb0c1a4edf9c92caf47b1e46f3cc69d15402` (M3A, card database facade,
merged). Branch: `m3/deck-model-ydk`. Final head: `955a1103278448d3bc9fc6f6b1f402ac4447db7b`.

Addresses exactly one M3 roadmap item: **"Deck model reading and writing `.ydk`"**. M3
remains in progress after this PR - the deck builder UI and fast search are not started.

- `edopro_next::data::Deck` (`data/include/edopro_next/data/deck.h`): three ordered
  `std::vector<data::CardCode>` - `main`/`extra`/`side`. No `CardDataC` pointers, no
  `CardDatabase`, no Qt/QML/Irrlicht/`ocgcore`/`gframe`, no legality or deck-size logic of
  any kind. Order and duplicates preserved exactly - never deduplicated, never sorted.
- A `.ydk` codec (`data/include/edopro_next/data/ydk.h`, `data/src/ydk.cpp`):
  `parse_ydk`/`load_ydk` (read) and `serialize_ydk`/`save_ydk` (write), separating pure
  text-to-value logic from filesystem I/O.
- A new CMake target, `edopro_next_deck` (`data/CMakeLists.txt`), deliberately separate from
  `edopro_next_data` - it links **no SQLite**, proven by its own test executable's link
  graph, not just documented.
- `docs/architecture/deck-model.md` - full source archaeology of
  `DeckManager::LoadCardList`/`LoadDeck`/`SaveDeck`/`MakeYdkEntryString`, with exact line
  citations against upstream `54ea755a`.
- `docs/adr/0004-deck-model-ydk-codec.md` - the four load-bearing decisions this PR makes.
- `data/tests/test_deck_ydk.cpp` - 37 tests, all passing.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `README.md`, `.github/workflows/edopro-next.yml` - status updates and
  a truthful CI job rename (see below).

## Source archaeology findings (full detail in `docs/architecture/deck-model.md`)

- `LoadCardList` (`gframe/deck_manager.cpp:272-318`) is the actual `.ydk` parser -
  `static`, private to that file. It never fails on file content, only on failing to open
  the file at all. CRLF is stripped by hand (`FileStream` is plain `std::fstream` on Linux,
  no text-mode translation). `#main` is inert - always. `#extra` is functional only
  when the caller supplies a non-null `extralist` pointer; any `!`-prefixed line (not just
  literal `"!side"`) permanently latches into the side section - once set, neither flag ever
  resets. A line is only ever attempted as a number if it contains a digit at all; parsing
  uses `std::stoul` exactly, whose sign/overflow/trailing-garbage/base-10 semantics were
  verified empirically against this project's actual Linux/g++ 15.2.0 baseline, not assumed.
- Upstream has two load modes, both reached from `LoadDeckFromFile`'s `separated` bool: with
  `separated = false` (the parameter's own default), `#extra` is inert and section
  membership is decided afterward by `LoadDeck`, which needs a live `CardDatabase` and
  classifies by card type (Fusion/Synchro/Xyz/Link/Ritual). With `separated = true`,
  `LoadCardList` itself splits by file markers - but `LoadDeck` still reclassifies
  afterward, moving an Extra-Deck-typed card out of `#main` regardless of which section the
  file put it in. Neither mode is fully determined by the file's own text without a
  database. Real callers overwhelmingly use `separated = true` (the deck builder's own
  file-open/drag-drop paths, `gframe/deck_con.cpp`).
- `SaveDeck` (two overloads, `gframe/deck_manager.cpp:436-468`) always writes
  `#main`/`#extra`/`!side` unconditionally, even for an empty section. `MakeYdkEntryString`
  optionally prefixes a name comment (`gGameConfig->addCardNamesToDeckList`, needs a
  database name lookup) and `SaveDeck` sources a `"#created by <nickname>"` line from live UI
  state (`mainGame->ebNickName`).
- Card code 0: `LoadCardList` itself has no special case for it - stores it structurally
  like any other code. The downstream, database-dependent `LoadDeck` step resolves an
  unrecognized code (0 included, since no real `.cdb` row has id 0) to a dummy `CardDataC`,
  and is mode-dependent: dropped in non-separated mode, kept as an untyped Main-deck
  placeholder in separated mode. The two upstream behaviours disagree with each other.

## Decisions this PR makes (ADR 0004)

- **Explicit sections are authoritative, not type-based auto-classification.** This codec
  always behaves as if `separated = true` were requested - `#extra`/`!` are always
  functional - and never performs `LoadDeck`'s card-type reclassification. No
  `CardDatabase` dependency anywhere in `parse_ydk`/`serialize_ydk`. A future,
  explicitly-reviewed layer with a live database can implement `LoadDeck`'s reclassification
  as a `Deck -> Deck` transformation on top of this codec.
- **Card code 0 is excluded during parsing, not stored.** Neither of upstream's two
  mode-dependent behaviours is reproduced; instead, a line parsing to `0` (including a value
  that wraps to `0` via `uint32_t` truncation, e.g. `2^32` on a 64-bit `unsigned long`) is
  dropped from the resulting `Deck` and reported via a non-fatal `YdkIgnoredLine`, consistent
  with `CardCode::None`'s established "not a real card" meaning from M3A
  (`data/include/edopro_next/data/card_code.h`). A magnitude that overflows `std::stoul`'s
  own range - which, depending on `unsigned long`'s width, `2^32` itself may or may not be;
  see "ABI-dependent parsing" below - is a separate, distinguishable case (`"malformed card
  code"`, not code 0), pinned by separate tests.
- **Unknown non-zero codes need no special handling.** Because `Deck` stores `CardCode`
  values rather than pointers into a catalogue, any syntactically valid code round-trips
  unchanged whether or not a database recognizes it - no dummy/alias mechanism needed.
- **The writer never depends on a card database or UI state.** `YdkWriteOptions::creator` is
  a plain optional string this codec never sources a value for; the legacy name-commented
  export form (`# CardName` then `<code>`) is deliberately not offered in any form, since it
  requires a card-name lookup this codec's boundary should not carry.

## Round-trip and failure guarantees

- `parse_ydk(serialize_ydk(deck)) == deck` for any `Deck` this codec produces, or any `Deck`
  containing only non-zero `CardCode` values - identical order, duplicates, and section
  membership, including unknown codes and the empty deck. Comments/whitespace are not
  expected to survive; this is a semantic round-trip, not a lossless text round-trip.
- **`CardCode::None` is explicitly outside this guarantee, by contract, not by accident.**
  `Deck`'s vectors are public, so a caller can construct one containing `CardCode::None`
  directly even though `parse_ydk` never produces one. `serialize_ydk` does not filter it -
  it is written as a literal `"0"` line like any other code - which `parse_ydk` then excludes
  under the same code-0 policy, so that specific `Deck` does not round-trip. This is now
  documented on `Deck` and `serialize_ydk` themselves and pinned by
  `a_deck_containing_card_code_none_does_not_round_trip`, rather than being an untested edge
  case a caller could stumble into unknowingly.
- `load_ydk` has the one genuine failure mode (file open/read); `parse_ydk` (in-memory text)
  cannot fail on content at all, matching `LoadCardList` itself. A failed `load_ydk` returns
  an empty `Deck` in a fresh result value - there is no in-place mutation of a caller-owned
  `Deck`, so a caller that only assigns on `ok == true` gets transactional behaviour for
  free (pinned by `loading_a_missing_file_fails_and_leaves_an_existing_deck_untouched`).
- `serialize_ydk`/`save_ydk` are deterministic: same `Deck` plus options produces
  byte-identical output, always `\n`, and `save_ydk` writes in binary mode.
- `save_ydk`'s success path is write, then flush, then close, each checked in turn - `ok` is
  only set once `close()` has itself succeeded, not merely once `write()`/`flush()` have.
  `load_ydk` reads through `file.read()` in a sized loop rather than direct streambuf
  insertion, so a genuine mid-read I/O error is detected via `file.bad()` rather than
  silently producing a truncated or empty `Deck` reported as success.

## ABI-dependent parsing: `std::stoul` on `4294967296` (2³²)

This codec calls `std::stoul` exactly as upstream's `LoadCardList` does, so it inherits
`std::stoul`'s own platform-dependent behaviour rather than normalizing it away. On this
project's current Linux baseline (64-bit `unsigned long`), `4294967296` parses successfully
and then truncates to `0` via `static_cast<uint32_t>`, landing on the code-0 policy above. On
a platform where `unsigned long` is exactly 32 bits (LLP64 - e.g. Windows, a stated future
target this project does not yet build for), `4294967296` does not fit in `unsigned long` at
all, so `std::stoul` itself throws `std::out_of_range` and the line is reported as malformed
instead. Both are upstream's own genuine per-platform `std::stoul` behaviour for the same
input; `data/tests/test_deck_ydk.cpp`'s
`two_to_the_32_is_excluded_one_way_or_another_depending_on_unsigned_long_width` branches on
`std::numeric_limits<unsigned long>::max()` at compile time and asserts whichever diagnostic
actually applies, always checking the one invariant that holds regardless: no card is stored.

## Tests: 37 (`data/tests/test_deck_ydk.cpp`), all passing

Canonical three-section parsing; empty-section and fully-empty round trips; duplicate/order
preservation; an arbitrary unknown non-zero code (no database involved anywhere in this
binary - it links no SQLite); comments and creator metadata never becoming cards; blank
lines; CRLF; a file with no trailing newline; a repeated `#extra` marker; any `!`-prefixed
line latching the side section, including the `!side` before `#extra` ordering that proves
the latch never resets; cards before any marker defaulting to main; `std::stoul`-relevant
cases pinned individually (leading-digit-then-garbage, surrounding whitespace, leading `+`,
leading `-` wrapping via unsigned arithmetic, a decimal point, a hex-looking `"0x1A"` prefix
parsing as decimal `0`, a magnitude far beyond any native integer width reported as malformed
on every conforming platform); code 0 excluded in every section; the ABI-portable `2^32`
boundary test above; the max valid `uint32_t` code; exact byte-for-byte writer output with
and without creator, and for a fully empty deck; a creator string with embedded newlines
sanitized byte-for-byte and proven unable to inject a card line end-to-end; `Deck` containing
`CardCode::None` proven not to round-trip, on purpose; parse-serialize-parse identity; real
file save/load round-trip; transactional failure on a missing file; deterministic repeated
serialization; two platform-conditional regression tests (each checks its special file exists
first, doing nothing on a platform without one) that write to `/dev/full` and read from
`/proc/self/mem` on Linux to prove the flush-failure and mid-read-failure detection actually
trigger, not just compile.

`edopro_next_data`'s existing 30 tests are unchanged and still pass (no regression).

## Module dependencies (verified, not just documented)

`edopro_next_deck`'s own test executable (`test_deck_ydk`) links `edopro_next_deck_test_main`
only - `ldd` on the built binary shows no `libsqlite3` anywhere in its link graph, distinct
from `edopro_next_data`/`test_card_database`, which do link SQLite.

## No legality, search, QML, or upstream-owned changes

No deck-size/three-copy/banlist/LFList/whitelist logic anywhere. No fast-search
indexing/filtering. No QML deck builder. No YDKe/Base64 codec (a genuinely separate format,
confirmed unrelated during archaeology - not needed here). No `gframe/` or `ocgcore/`
changes of any kind - both were read from, never written to.

## CI

The existing `card-database` job (id unchanged) now also builds and runs
`edopro_next_deck`/`test_deck_ydk`, since both live in the same `data/CMakeLists.txt` and
`data/build` tree - its display name is changed from "Card database facade" to **"Card and
deck data"** to stay truthful about what it covers. Expected jobs on this PR: Regression
harness (3.10, 3.12), Card and deck data, Semantic client model, Qt 6 shell,
Upstream EDOPro baseline (observer=false, observer=true).

## Review fixes landed since this PR opened

Two rounds of automated/external review, both fully addressed on the current head:

- **Round 1** (buffered-write failure, `rdbuf()`-based read failure, creator newline
  injection): `save_ydk` originally checked the stream right after `write()`, which can
  report `good()` even though a full filesystem only fails at flush time; `load_ydk`
  originally read via `buffer << file.rdbuf()`, which bypasses `basic_istream::read()`'s
  state-update machinery and can leave a genuine mid-read I/O error undetected; `creator`
  was emitted verbatim, so an embedded newline could inject a phantom card line into the
  output. All three confirmed empirically (`/dev/full`, `/proc/self/mem`, and a direct
  parse-back of injected output) before fixing, and pinned by dedicated tests.
- **Round 2** (this pass): `save_ydk` also now checks `close()`, not just `flush()`, before
  reporting success; the `2^32` test is now ABI-portable rather than assuming a 64-bit
  `unsigned long`; `Deck`'s `CardCode::None` round-trip precondition is now explicit and
  pinned rather than an implicit, untested consequence of the code-0 policy.

## Known limitations / deliberately deferred work

- `LoadDeck`'s type-based Extra-Deck reclassification is not reproduced anywhere - by
  design (ADR 0004, Decision 2). A `Deck` parsed from a file whose author put a Fusion
  monster in `#main` will keep it there; upstream's own loader would move it.
- No end-to-end proof that upstream EDOPro's actual binary opens a file this codec wrote -
  the format-level claim is supported by construction (writer matches `SaveDeck`'s section
  syntax exactly; the writer's own output round-trips through this codec's parser
  unchanged; `LoadCardList` is `static`/private and cannot be linked directly for a real
  cross-check without a large legacy harness this PR deliberately does not build), not by a
  GUI integration test.
- The legacy name-commented export feature and creator-nickname sourcing are not
  implemented at all (ADR 0004, Decision 4) - a caller wanting them composes on top.
- `save_ydk`'s `close()`-failure path has no portable way to be forced in a unit test (the
  existing `/dev/full` case already fails at the flush step, before `close()` is reached) -
  the fix is standard-guaranteed (`std::basic_fstream::close()` sets `failbit` on failure)
  rather than test-proven for that specific step.
